summary: Our project is an interactive digital museum showcasing NASA’s retired and historic spacecraft. Instead of static displays, it provides a tailored, immersive educational experience for each device—allowing users to explore its components, mission timeline, and scientific achievements. Built using modern digital design tools and official NASA open-source archives, our platform makes space engineering engaging and accessible to inspire students in STEM. Unlike traditional galleries, our creative "device-centric" approach turns every abandoned spacecraft into a standalone interactive lesson, designed with a strong focus on scientific accuracy, visual appeal, and user-friendly navigation.
details:
:

Our project is an interactive digital museum dedicated to exploring NASA’s historic and retired space hardware, satellites, and rovers. Instead of merely displaying static photos, the platform offers a comprehensive, immersive educational experience tailored to each specific device. Users can virtually inspect the spacecraft, explore its internal components, understand its mission timeline, and discover the scientific breakthroughs it achieved.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

The museum makes complex space engineering and history accessible, engaging, and easy to understand for students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide. By bringing retired space missions back to life digitally, our project aims to bridge the gap in STEM education, spark curiosity in space exploration, and inspire the next generation of engineers and scientists.
